newsitem.title: DENMARK: FORECAST - Carlsberg H1 profit seen up 9.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Carlsberg H1 profit seen up 9.6 pct.

text.p: Brewer Carlsberg is expected to report a 14 percent rise in operating results and a 9.6 percent increase in pre-tax profits when it publishes 1996/1997 first-half results next week.

The consensus of seven analysts' forecasts was a rise in pre-tax profit to 812 million crowns from 741 million in the first half of 1995/1996 and growth in the operating result to 606 million crowns from last year's 530 million.
Forecasts for pre-tax profit ranged from a high of 885 million to a low of 710 million, while those for the operating result ran from 650 million down to 575 million.
Gross turnover was on average seen up to 8.99 billion crowns, from 8.53 billion in 1995/96, with forecasts ranging between 9.2 billion and 8.75 billion.

The analysts said the company's future progress would depend to a large extent on U.K. regulators' decision on the proposed sale of British joint venture Carlsberg-Tetley to Bass, which currently owns half.

"It is very uncertain if the buyout will be approved or, if it is approved, if there will be such strict conditions attached that Bass will choose to drop the deal," said one analyst, who requested anonymity.
"If the sale is not approved it will be a serious blow for Carlsberg and will also be reflected in the share price," another analyst said.
The share closed on Friday at 385 crowns and the analysts forecast that approval of the Bass deal could send it up to around 450 crowns, while rejection could drag it down to 370.

Several analysts agreed that the current share price assumes approval of both the Bass sale and a proposed Nordic soft-drink distribution agreement with Coca Cola, currently under review by EU competition authorities. -- Joern Nurkka, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
